Benchmark coaching — DQ-reason activity standards (primary) & tier bars (secondary)

Benchmarks = the average calls + emails logged on qualified prospects in each tier (the effort it actually took to get a Yes). A closed prospect is Below if its activity is under 75% of its tier bar (risk of disqualifying too quickly), Above if over 125% (over-contacting / pest risk), else On. Percentages and the per-rep table reflect the current filters (set above) and cover closed prospects only (qualified + disqualified), excluding test/internal.

Methodology & anomaly notes

Phone activity comes from Salesforce Task activity (TaskSubtype='Call') linked to the prospect's Contact (WhoId), its Account (WhatId), or the Prospect record itself (WhatId) — deduped by Task Id and window-scoped to each prospect's created→close life. This matters because the large majority of calls are logged against the Account (about 6.4k account-linked call tasks vs 1.6k contact-linked), so a contact-only view drastically under-counted phone activity. Top-line call totals count each Task once (an account call shared by sibling prospects isn't multiplied); per-prospect rows show every call on their contact/account/record during their window.

Emails (merged source). Prospect emails are the union of the uploaded CSV export (email_export_20260831.csv, matched by contact email) and Salesforce email tasks (TaskSubtype='Email') linked to the prospect's Contact, Account, or Prospect record, deduped to the minute so a send logged in more than one place is counted once. This captures emails logged in Salesforce but missing from the CSV and vice-versa: 344 prospects have email activity only Salesforce had, 530 have it in both. CSV coverage: 1,834 of 2,087 CSV addresses matched a cohort prospect (253 unmatched, belonging to other cohorts, unlinked contacts, or excluded records). Emails are counted only within each prospect's open→close window (created date to close, or to today for still-open prospects) using per-email timestamps; sends before the record existed or after it closed are excluded from the activity count and benchmark and surfaced as anomalies. (This fixes an earlier CSV-only build that under-counted emails logged only in Salesforce.)

Record freshness. Every refresh re-pulls stage, tier, disqualification reason and close date for the entire cohort from Salesforce (not just newly-created prospects), so a record's stage/outcome on the dashboard always matches Salesforce. Past activity that already occurred (calls, emails, meetings) is immutable, but the record's current state is never locked.

Open opportunities = count and sum(Amount) of Opportunity records with IsClosed=false on the prospect's related Account.

Disqualification activity standards (Inbound Leads Activity Standards, p.2). Each disqualified record is judged against the minimum required for its disqualification reason, not its tier. No Show / Unable to Reach (our Unresponsive reason) require 4 emails + 4 calls with voicemail; the qualification reasons (Not Government Focused, Only Bids Focused, Budget, Competitor, Not a Decision Maker) require two-way communication — approximated as a logged call over one minute (via MAX(CallDurationInSeconds)) or a held meeting, since confirmed inbound email replies aren't captured yet (a two-way-email CSV can be dropped in later to strengthen this); False Lead maps to Invalid Lead and needs no contact. Reasons with no document standard (Other, Unsubscribed, Automation Expired — 411 records) are shown but not scored and should be given a defined standard. Tier bars remain as a secondary view of average qualified activity.

“Pass to the SDR” sequencing (issue flagged). On p.2 the “Pass to the SDR” step appears after the 4 emails + 4 calls-with-voicemail and only for No Show / Unable to Reach — i.e., a record should be passed to an SDR only once that activity minimum is met and the record is disqualified, never before. Records disqualified as Unresponsive that did not meet the 4+4 minimum are flagged “pass-to-SDR premature” (currently 183 of 183 Unresponsive DQs). Note this count is inflated by the voicemail-logging gap below, so treat it as “needs manager review” rather than a hard violation. We do not yet have an explicit “passed to SDR” field in the pull; if one exists we can detect the hand-off directly.

Speed-to-Lead (doc p.1). The S2L column (right of Created) shows whether the first outreach met the tier SLA — 24 hours for Tier 1 / Tier 2, 2 business days for Tier 3, 5 business days for Tier 4 — and the First activity column shows the true first-touch date/time driving it. First activity is the earliest logged email or call at/after the record was created (from per-email timestamps and MIN(CreatedDate) on call tasks); meetings are treated as downstream outcomes and excluded from first-touch. “No activity” means no qualifying email/call was logged after creation (no S2L credit). Overall this cohort: 1,133 met · 386 late · 493 no activity, of 2,012 SLA-eligible records.

Manager review workflow. Each disqualified record has a Reviewed checkbox, and every record has a free-text Notes field (rightmost column). Both are saved in your browser and survive reloads/rebuilds on this machine; the DQ review filter narrows to reviewed / unreviewed disqualified records so a manager can work the queue to zero. Export reviews + notes downloads prospect_reviews.json (reviewed IDs + notes) — drop it into source_data/ and the next rebuild treats it as the committed baseline (shareable across machines and reportable).

Anomaly logic: emails predating prospect creation; emails continuing >1 day after a prospect was disqualified/closed (cadence overrun); a contact email attached to more than one prospect record; test/internal records ("test" in name/company/email or company = GovSpend); and prospects with in-window email activity but zero logged calls. Zero outreach (no calls and no in-window emails) is split into closed cold — a prospect closed/disqualified with no logged touch, the meaningful gap — and unworked (open) — a still-open prospect not yet worked (largely brand-new / auto-created records).

Data provenance & refresh model. Rendered Sep 1 2026, 11:46 AM from the frozen snapshot (source: Salesforce Prospect__c created Jun 1 – Aug 31 2026, Task call & email activity linked by Contact/Account/Prospect record, Event meetings, Opportunity; emails also merge email_export_20260831.csv). Current snapshot: 2,012 prospects, 1,435 calls, 5,400 in-window emails, 1,834/2,087 CSV emails matched (253 unmatched), 414 open opps, 7 test/internal excluded from benchmarks. Excluded from this output entirely (removed from every figure): reps Evan White, Arjun Sahai, and Marc Digeronimo, plus any record whose company is GovSpend (internal test records) — this is why some CSV emails now show as unmatched. Each row is tagged with its Department (Sales / RM) and Manager per the current roster. Past activity is frozen — calls, emails and meetings that already occurred are immutable and are never recomputed; closed prospects are locked. Refreshes are append-only: new/changed prospects and any new activity are added to the snapshot and only still-open prospects are re-checked. No values are hard-coded — every number is derived from the snapshot at render time, and anything unavailable (empty SF rollups, tiers/reps with too few qualified prospects to set a bar) is labeled rather than estimated.

Buckets: Trend / grid metric: Time axis = prospect created date · reflects every filter above · recent buckets have more still-open prospects (immature outcome rates).

Per-rep coaching grid — by (created)

Each cell is the selected metric for that rep's prospects created in that period. % meeting tier bar and qualification / disqualification rate cover closed prospects; % DQ meeting DQ standard covers disqualified prospects with a defined standard; avg activity covers all prospects. Green = stronger, red = weaker (inverted for disqualification rate). The sparkline shows the rep's trend across periods. Everything here honors the filters at the top of the page — filter to a rep, tier, team or timeframe and the charts and grid update live.
